claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 3. Every schema lookup under a rule set makes MySQL read the whole data dictionary. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:349` and `:353` wrap `TABLE_SCHEMA`, `TABLE_NAME`, `COLUMN_NAME` and the three referenced-side columns in `CAST(... AS BINARY)` before comparing them. A function applied to a column stops the optimizer using that column for lookups, so the derived table built in `_catalog_body` has no usable restriction and must read every schema and table the SQL Lens database user can see, and `_MATERIALIZE_LIMIT` then forces that whole result into a temporary table. The new prompt sentence sends every schema lookup down this path, and neither the unit tests nor the connector tests measure it — the connector fixture has five small tables in one database. The reviewer did not benchmark it; the mechanism is visible in the generated SQL pinned by `tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:1161-1183`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
